A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSR-Bench study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination and bibliography changes.

before.justification: V3 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs, including prompting, spatial, narrative, code-generation and strategy-selection experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds prompting controls, error analyses, structural edit-distance results and original analysis of collected benchmark scores.

M1.justification: The benchmark's task-generation procedures, structural operations, ground-truth construction and main prompting/output pipeline remain unchanged. Added prompting comparators and auxiliary evaluation metrics do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The 20-structure, 35-operation, 4,140-instance DSR suite and Appendix L scenarios remain. Appendix M extends secondary evaluation coverage using collected scores from LiveBench, TableBench, SWE-Bench, LiveCodeBench, GSO Bench and AgentBench; it does not establish new model executions on those tasks. Table 5's changed challenge markers reconcile coverage already represented in existing results.

E2.justification: Appendix E.2 and Table 25 add Plan-and-Solve, Self-Consistency and Least-to-Most to the prompting comparisons and include the previously studied CodeEnforce alongside them. This is a bounded expansion on selected tasks; the main 13-model comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 adds a GPT-5 control removing the token-budget instruction, structural edit-distance evaluation and protocols for correlating overlapping models' benchmark scores. Reported totals change from 166,230 to 161,460 evaluations and from 1,624 to 1,620 schema trials, consistent with the stated component counts. These corrections do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands diagnostic analysis: additional prompting and token-instruction controls (E.2–E.3), zero-score failures across models and tasks (E.4), code-error inspection (H), partial structural recovery (I.2), and downstream benchmark alignment (M). The earlier spatial-shift, paraphrasing and strategy-selection analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing three-run mean-and-standard-deviation practice remains. Table 33 adds distributional reporting through interquartile ranges and standard deviations across 30 instances, alongside Figure 10's histograms. No increased repetition count, new seed policy or confidence intervals are established.

E6.justification: Main Tables 2–4 remain unchanged, including GPT-5's 0.46 challenge score. Table 6 corrects nine Queue cells; GPT-4.1 short changes from 0.97 to 0.82, matching the retained Table 12. Substantial new results include prompting controls, distinct zero-score failures, RB-tree/KD-tree edit scores of 0.66 despite exact accuracies of 0.14/0.04, and benchmark correlations such as Spearman 0.97 for LiveCodeBench versus 0.30 for AgentBench. These are added analyses, not same-setting model improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix I.2 introduces mathematical definitions of normalized tree-edit similarity and graph edge-disagreement similarity under a fixed-node-set assumption. V3's auxiliary metric discussion covers string Levenshtein distance only. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V4 narrows the measurement claim to operational structural generalization, explicitly describing it as necessary but insufficient for broader algorithmic reasoning. The benchmark's novelty claim, principal contributions and headline performance findings remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds substantive boundaries concerning instance-level versus task-level contamination, final-answer-only scoring, hallucination classification and the inability to cleanly separate reasoning from pattern matching. Sections 4.3, E.4, H and I.2 also distinguish structure extraction from execution, explain different zero-score mechanisms and interpret partial structural recovery. These materially refine the earlier failure interpretations.

D1.justification: New details include three Self-Consistency rollouts, manually designed Least-to-Most decomposition and the leaderboard-score selection procedure in Appendix M. V4 explicitly clarifies final-answer-only evaluation. Some new experiments, particularly Table 25, still lack clear model and setting identification; existing code/data access information remains.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting prompting comparisons, contamination qualifications and downstream benchmark analysis, including Program of Thoughts, Plan-and-Solve, Self-Consistency, Least-to-Most, AgentBench, TableBench and GSO. It also adds a distinct DeepSeek-R1 reference. Positioning against CLRS-Text, NLGraph and GraphQA remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand the benchmark acronym, rename difficulty levels as length levels, refine explanatory passages and update publication information. Section 5 gains a limitations block, and appendices gain subsections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative organization are retained.

P2.justification: New appendix displays comprise Tables 25–27, 33, 38–40 and Figure 10. Existing figures and main table designs remain, with local relocations, annotation corrections and caption refinements. Abbreviated author lists compact the bibliography; the document's overall visual style is retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves accuracy through Table 6 and count corrections, strengthens diagnostics through E.4 and I.2, and makes reasoning and contamination boundaries clearer in Section 5. The gains are limited by incomplete settings for some added experiments, correlations based on only 4–10 overlapping models without uncertainty estimates, and retained broad memorization interpretations.
